blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Revolt of 1857 began on May 10, 1857, at Meerut by sepoys of the 20th Native Infantry and quickly spread across North and Central India.
The immediate trigger was the introduction of the Enfield Rifle with greased cartridges reported to contain fat from cows and pigs.
Bahadur Shah II (Zafar) was proclaimed 'Shahenshah-e-Hindustan' as the symbolic leader of the uprising.
Key leaders included Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi), Nana Saheb and Tantia Tope (Kanpur), Begum Hazrat Mahal (Lucknow), and Kunwar Singh (Bihar).
The uprising resulted in the end of East India Company rule and established direct rule under the British Crown via the Government of India Act 1858.

blocks.content: The Revolt of 1857 was the first major, widespread challenge to British rule in India. It marked a turning point in Indian history as it exposed the deep resentment of Indian soldiers, peasants, rulers, and common people against the policies of the British East India Company. Although the revolt failed militarily, it shook the foundations of British rule and led to significant administrative, political, and military changes. For SSC examinations, the Revolt of 1857 is a HIGH-WEIGHTAGE topic and questions are asked from its causes, centres, leaders, nature, failure, and consequences.

Historians have described the Revolt of 1857 in different ways. British historians initially called it a 'Sepoy Mutiny'. Indian historians like V.D. Savarkar termed it the 'First War of Indian Independence'. In reality, it was a combination of a sepoy mutiny, peasant uprising, and princely resistance.

The British followed aggressive policies of expansion that alienated Indian rulers. The Doctrine of Lapse led to the annexation of states like Jhansi, Satara, and Nagpur. The annexation of Awadh in 1856 hurt the interests of taluqdars and soldiers.
Here lay the woman who was the only man among the rebels.
British administration was corrupt, rigid, and insensitive to Indian traditions. High posts were reserved for Europeans, creating resentment among Indians.
British land revenue policies ruined peasants and zamindars. Heavy taxation, destruction of traditional industries, and drain of wealth caused widespread poverty.
British social reforms were viewed with suspicion. Activities of Christian missionaries and laws like the Widow Remarriage Act created fear that the British intended to destroy Indian religions.
Indian sepoys were discriminated against in pay and promotion. The General Service Enlistment Act required overseas service, offending religious sentiments.

blocks.content: The immediate cause was the introduction of Enfield rifles whose cartridges were greased with cow and pig fat. Sepoys had to bite these cartridges, hurting both Hindu and Muslim sentiments.

The revolt began on 10 May 1857 at Meerut when Indian soldiers rose against their British officers. They marched to Delhi and proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar as the Emperor of India. The revolt quickly spread to North and Central India, covering areas like Awadh, Kanpur, Jhansi, Bihar, and parts of Madhya Pradesh.

items: Frequently tested: Mapping centers of revolt to their rebel leaders and corresponding British officers who suppressed them (e.g., Jhansi - Hugh Rose, Delhi - John Nicholson).
Note for Prelims: The educated middle class, modern intelligentsia, and most Indian princely rulers largely stayed neutral or supported the British.
Lord Canning became the last Governor-General of the East India Company and the first Viceroy of India under Crown Rule.

blocks.content: The Revolt of 1857 failed due to lack of unity, poor organisation, absence of modern weapons, and lack of support from southern India and princely states like Hyderabad and Kashmir. The British were better organised, had superior resources, and controlled communications.

The revolt ended the rule of the East India Company. The Government of India Act, 1858 transferred power to the British Crown. The policy of annexation was abandoned and the Indian army was reorganised.
The Revolt of 1857 marked the beginning of a new phase in Indian nationalism. It exposed the exploitative nature of British rule and inspired later freedom movements.
Revolt of 1857 began at Meerut | Last Mughal Emperor – Bahadur Shah Zafar | Leader of Kanpur – Nana Sahib | Rani of Jhansi – Lakshmibai | Immediate cause – Greased cartridges
